title: Extending a derived stalk isomorphism between existing perfect models
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and x a point, with derived categories of its module sheaves, their restrictions, and stalk modules [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Let G,H be global module-sheaf complexes. Suppose Q(G) has a strictly perfect representative on a neighborhood of x [def-pc-perfect-complex], and H restricted to an open U containing x is strictly perfect. Given an isomorphism Q(G_x) -> Q(H_x) in the derived category of stalk modules, there is an affine open W containing x with W contained in U and an isomorphism Q(G restricted to W) -> Q(H restricted to W). H is fixed; no new complex, degree bounds or prescribed ranks are constructed.

source.place: Tag 09RE affine full faithfulness proof; More on Algebra Tag 0BC7 (2); Tags 00CR and 06Z0

proof.text: 1. Choose an affine neighbourhood inside the two given neighbourhoods, restrict the strictly perfect models, and apply the derived stalk Hom-lifting lemma to the given stalk isomorphism. It produces a smaller affine open and an actual chain map whose derived stalk image is the prescribed morphism.

2. The derived image of the lifted chain map on the stalk is a composite of isomorphisms, hence the stalk chain map is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the perfect stalk quasi-isomorphism detection lemma to obtain a further affine open where the restricted chain map is a quasi-isomorphism.

3. Restrict both derived model comparisons to the final affine open and compose their inverses with the derived image of the quasi-isomorphism. The result is the required derived isomorphism between the restrictions of G and H.

mathlib_searches.results: Two searches, eight hits each. Ordinary stalk restriction isomorphisms, Tilde.stalkIso, scheme spreading-out, and stalkwise isomorphism detection; no bounded complex lift or local derived-isomorphism extension.

Mathlib has rankAtStalk, free loci and ordinary stalk isomorphisms, but no complex lifting or local derived comparison. Project finite-free stalk lifting modules start with two existing complexes, use Scheme.Modules/pullback, and the homotopy-spreading theorem compares with a single-degree complex. Internal-Hom stalk localization requires a Noetherian scheme and coherent degree-zero source, so does not apply here.
